question.text: The Black-Scholes option pricing model requires which of the following inputs?

answer.text: Spot price, strike price, time to expiry, risk-free rate, and volatility
Spot price, strike price, time to expiry, dividend yield, and trading volume
Strike price, futures price, open interest, volatility, and interest rate
Spot price, market sentiment, lot size, trading volume, and margin requirement

explanation.text: The Logic: The Black-Scholes model uses five inputs (workbook pages 75 and 79): the stock/spot price (S), strike price (X), time to expiration (T), risk-free interest rate (r) and volatility of the underlying (sigma). The basic call-price calculation in the workbook ignores dividends. The Trap: Trading volume, open interest, lot size, market sentiment and margin requirement are market microstructure variables, not Black-Scholes inputs. The model is theoretical and uses only the five variables listed above. Note: Of the five inputs, all are directly observable except volatility, which has to be estimated.
